lead.title: Perennial grasses show how crops could stop leaving nitrogen in the field
lead.summary: A Plant Cell study built a transcriptomic atlas of senescence from 2,685 RNA-seq libraries covering 14 field-grown Panicoideae grasses across two seasons, with maize and sorghum as annual references. The gene networks that strip nitrogen from ageing leaves turned out to be shared by annuals and perennials, but the networks that let perennials park that nitrogen in rhizomes and roots, linked to seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance, have diverged in annual crops. Because 30 to 50% of maize nitrogen stays in residue where it can be lost, the authors offer these conserved candidates as a route to perennial-style nutrient recycling in annual crops, though no engineered crop has yet been tested.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Regulatory atlases lead today: a 2,685-library grass senescence atlas, a plum ripening regulome built from DNase-seq and DAP-seq, and a wheat grain spatial transcriptome that places adhesion-linked FLA genes in the crease, a possible lever for flour extraction.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Tools for less-studied crops: an 82% efficient hairy root system for peanut, the first VIGS system for sponge gourd (77% of plants silenced), a 10-SNP dragon fruit ID panel, and the RAGNAROK annotation pipeline benchmarked against BRAKER3.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Relevant threads for prairie systems: HvNCED12 knockouts in barley lost salt tolerance at 150 mM NaCl, a 33-year study found nitrogen fertiliser eroded rhizobium benefit to legumes, and Kernza endophyte trials showed host genotype decides inoculant benefit. Links to prairie fields are my inference; none was a Canadian field study.

plant.title: A 2,685-library atlas shows how perennial grasses bank nitrogen underground at senescence
plant.summary: Researchers sequenced 2,685 RNA-seq libraries from field-grown leaves, roots, stalks and rhizomes of 14 Panicoideae grasses across two seasons, using maize and sorghum as annual references. Networks that move nitrogen out of senescing leaves were conserved between annuals and perennials, but networks that build underground sinks, tied to seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance, had diverged in annual crop accessions. The authors propose these genes as targets to cut the 30 to 50% of maize nitrogen left behind in residue.

plant.title: A position-resolved regulatory map of plum ripening puts PsEIN3-1 at the top of a sugar cascade
plant.summary: Combining transcriptomes, DNase-seq chromatin accessibility and DAP-seq for ripening transcription factors from six families, the study built a regulatory network for Prunus salicina fruit ripening. The ethylene factor PsEIN3-1 binds the promoters of PsbZIP44 and PsNAC1, which in turn target genes for ethylene synthesis, starch breakdown and sugar accumulation; the PsbZIP44 role was only preliminarily tested by transient transformation. Comparisons with peach, apricot and sweet cherry found conserved circuits, and the data are released as a Prunus Regulome Atlas.

plant.title: A CsCOP1, CsHY5 and CsGGT2 cascade sets theanine levels in tea
plant.summary: QTL mapping in an albino tea population identified CsCOP1, and silencing it reduced theanine while overexpression raised it. CsCOP1 ubiquitinates CsHY5 at lysine 428, lowering HY5 protein, repressing the theanine-hydrolysing gene CsGGT2 and slowing theanine breakdown in leaves. A non-synonymous CsGGT2 variant changed hydrolysing activity in natural populations, giving a candidate marker for breeding high-theanine cultivars.

plant.title: HvNCED12, switched on by HvMYB10, supports salt tolerance in barley
plant.summary: CRISPR knockout and overexpression lines of HvNCED12 in barley cv. Golden Promise were grown at 150 mM NaCl for 14 days. Salt induced the gene about sixfold within 24 hours; knockouts had less ABA and chlorophyll, 49.3% more malondialdehyde, poorer Na+/K+ balance and lower biomass, while overexpressors showed the opposite, and 100 µM ABA partly rescued the knockouts. HvMYB10 binds and activates the HvNCED12 promoter. These are controlled-environment results without field data.

plant.title: Spatial transcriptomics of the wheat grain points to crease FLA proteins in bran adhesion
plant.summary: A spatial transcriptomic atlas of Triticum aestivum grain at 14 days post-anthesis split the seed into pericarp, starchy endosperm, transfer cells, crease and embryo, and found 4,682 region-exclusive gene loci across 1,751 functional categories. Fasciclin-like arabinogalactan protein (FLA) transcripts were concentrated in the crease and linked to cell wall remodelling genes. The authors suggest silencing crease FLAs could loosen bran from endosperm and raise flour extraction, a hypothesis not yet tested in milling trials.

plant.title: Sugar transporter HaSWEET14 partners with florigen HaFT4 to time sunflower flowering under low light
plant.summary: Transcriptomes of sunflower grown at different light intensities identified HaSWEET14, a SWEET sugar transporter strongly suppressed by low light. In transient assays, silencing HaSWEET14 delayed flowering by 8 days and silencing HaFT4 by about 10 days, while overexpression of either sped flowering. The two proteins interact at the plasma membrane, suggesting a sugar transporter to florigen link in shade-delayed flowering of this oil crop.

plant.title: Mycorrhizal fungi did not shield native grasses from combined heat and drought
plant.summary: Six Australian native grasses with C<sub>3</sub> or C<sub>4</sub> photosynthesis were exposed to a simulated heatwave with and without water stress, with and without arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi. Combined heat and drought did more damage than either stress alone, and AM fungi did not improve performance, instead lowering transpiration under stress. C<sub>4</sub> grasses outperformed C<sub>3</sub> grasses, and both were more resilient in spring than in winter.

plant.title: NtWRKY11 raises cold tolerance in tobacco through ABA, calcium and CBF signalling
plant.summary: The nuclear transcription factor NtWRKY11 is induced by cold and drought, and overexpressing it reduced electrolyte leakage and reactive oxygen species while keeping germination and photosynthesis higher under cold. Transcriptome and physiology data suggest it promotes the ABA biosynthesis genes NCED3 and AAO3, feeding calcium signalling and the CBF to COR cold cascade, and boosts antioxidant enzymes. Several links in the proposed pathway are inferred from expression data rather than shown directly.

plant.title: ANAC030 speeds leaf senescence through jasmonate, cell death and chlorophyll genes in Arabidopsis
plant.summary: Inducible overexpression of the NAC factor ANAC030 accelerated leaf senescence and dominant repression delayed it, with jasmonic acid levels moving in the same directions. ChIP, EMSA and reporter assays showed ANAC030 binds promoters of genes for programmed cell death, chlorophyll breakdown and jasmonate synthesis, and genetic tests in nye1 and lox2 backgrounds supported direct regulation. This is an Arabidopsis-only result.

plant.title: Spotlight: 33 years of nitrogen fertiliser eroded the legume to rhizobium partnership
plant.summary: This commentary highlights a study by Bedwell and colleagues showing a mutualism meltdown in legume and rhizobium symbioses after 33 years of nitrogen fertilisation. Long-read sequencing revealed a mixed community of nodulating and non-nodulating Rhizobiaceae, in which a beneficial symbiont fell both in abundance and in the share of host-beneficial alleles. It is a short commentary; readers should consult the original study for effect sizes.

biotech.title: RAGNAROK, a GPU-accelerated Nextflow pipeline, beats BRAKER3 on plant gene annotation
biotech.summary: RAGNAROK bundles ab initio prediction, transcript and protein evidence, repeat masking, functional assignment and quality checks into one reproducible Nextflow and Apptainer workflow. Across seven reference-quality plant genomes it achieved higher sensitivity, precision and F1 than BRAKER3 at exon, transcript and gene levels when UTRs were included, ran faster, and improved BUSCO completeness when re-annotating five Rosaceae genomes. The code is open on GitHub; the benchmark was run by the tool's developers.

biotech.title: A cut-dipping hairy root method reaches 82% transformation in peanut and implicates miR319 in nitrate response
biotech.summary: Small RNA sequencing of peanut roots under low and high nitrogen found 9 and 99 candidate differentially expressed miRNAs after 5 and 10 days, and 114 negatively correlated miRNA and mRNA pairs. The team built a cut-dipping hairy root transformation system with up to 82.22% efficiency and used it to show that silencing miR319 promoted root elongation under high but not low nitrogen. TCP3 is proposed, not yet proven, as the miR319 target.

biotech.title: First VIGS system for sponge gourd silences genes in 77% of plants
biotech.summary: Sponge gourd had no reverse genetics tool, so the authors tested an apple stem grooving virus based pSMIL vector carrying a cucumber PDS fragment as a photobleaching reporter. The antisense construct bleached leaves by 18 days post-inoculation versus 21 days for sense, and silenced 77% of plants. Recombinant virus spread by sap inoculation gave systemic, persistent silencing without transgenic plants.

biotech.title: Timed supplemental lighting lifts plant-made vaccine yield in dense Nicotiana benthamiana stands
biotech.summary: In vertical-farm cultivation at 800 plants per square metre, self-shading cuts recombinant protein content per plant. Adding side lighting at half the top-light power both before and after gene transfer gave the highest yields per area of an influenza haemagglutinin antigen and an antibody. Yield per unit of lighting energy rose 16 to 26% over unlit controls.

biotech.title: Review: from oil biosynthesis to precision breeding of fatty acid profiles in oilseeds
biotech.summary: This review traces how plastidial synthesis, ER desaturation and elongation, acyl editing and triacylglycerol assembly set fatty acid composition in major and specialty oilseeds. It surveys how linkage mapping, GWAS, pangenomes and omics are finding canonical genes and new structural variants, and lays out a pipeline from locus discovery to allele choice, targeted editing and multigene engineering. The authors stress that AI-designed enzymes and edits still need biochemical validation and field testing.

biotech.title: StWRKY70 directly activates StAOS to defend potato against early blight
biotech.summary: Silencing StWRKY70 by VIGS made potato more susceptible to Alternaria solani and lowered jasmonic acid and antioxidant enzyme activity, while overexpression did the reverse. DAP-seq identified the jasmonate biosynthesis gene StAOS (allene oxide synthase) as a target, and yeast one-hybrid, EMSA and luciferase assays confirmed StWRKY70 binds and activates its promoter. Resistance was measured in controlled inoculations, not field trials.

biotech.title: A 10-SNP panel identifies dragon fruit accessions with 100% accuracy
biotech.summary: SLAF-seq of 45 Selenicereus accessions yielded 1,206,498 high-quality SNPs, resolved three genetic groups and corrected several misclassified accessions. A hierarchical marker set was built, and a 10-SNP ultra-core panel discriminated accessions with 100% accuracy in independent validation, overcoming misleading flesh colour in hybrids. Four candidate genes, including bHLH and MATE transporter genes, co-expressed with the betalain genes CYP76AD1-1 and DODA1.

biotech.title: One Rhizoctonia solani isolate carries ten new RNA viruses, including a record-size hypovirus
biotech.summary: Re-sequencing a single Brazilian R. solani isolate from zoysiagrass patch disease extended seven known viral genomes and uncovered ten novel RNA viruses across six families and the phylum Ambiviricota. Rhizoctonia solani hypovirus 1, over 25 kb, is the largest genome reported in Hypoviridae and carries a helicase domain suggestive of horizontal gene transfer. Such mycoviruses are candidates for future biocontrol screening, though none was tested for hypovirulence here.

biotech.title: Two new vitiviruses turn up in Brazil's pineapple genebank
biotech.summary: High-throughput sequencing of accessions in the Embrapa pineapple germplasm bank recovered three genomes of pineapple virus A, about 97% identical to the only previous sequence from Reunion Island, plus two new vitiviruses named pineapple vitivirus B and C. A new RT-PCR assay found all three widespread in the open-field collection. The tools support virus screening and sanitation of planting material.

biotech.title: Thermophilic Bacillus subtilis LSG20 protects rice seedlings from heat, likely via the protein TasA
biotech.summary: Culture filtrate of LSG20 grown at 28 °C protected rice seedlings from heat better than filtrate grown at 45 or 60 °C, so protection did not track the strain's own heat adaptation. The amyloid protein TasA was more abundant in 28 °C filtrate, and recombinant TasA improved seedling performance under heat and PEG osmotic stress. Results are from seedling assays only.

ag.title: A new Alternaria forma specialis causes leaf spot on California lettuce
ag.summary: A leaf spot with concentric rings appeared on coastal California lettuce in 2023, and all 15 tested iceberg, romaine, leaf and butterhead cultivars were susceptible. Of 22 other crops in seven families, only endive, potato and tomato developed disease, and genome sequencing placed the pathogen as a new forma specialis within the potato early blight species complex, distinct from the potato pathogen. The fungus forms microsclerotia that can start infection, and a near telomere-to-telomere genome is provided.

ag.title: Resistant rice plus Metarhizium kept brown planthopper from adapting across generations
ag.summary: Over multiple generations, chemical insecticides drove resistance and host adaptation in Nilaparvata lugens, while the fungus Metarhizium anisopliae CQMa421 combined with resistant rice IR36 kept the pest susceptible. Combined exposure activated AMPK in the fat body, shifting lipids toward immunity and away from detoxification and reproduction. These are laboratory results; field durability is untested.

ag.title: Geraniol from resistant Manchurian ash, in a slow-release microemulsion, targets emerald ash borer adults
ag.summary: Phloem metabolomics found the monoterpene geraniol enriched in resistant Fraxinus mandschurica versus susceptible F. velutina. A 57 nm oil-in-water microemulsion lowered LC50 and LD50 against Agrilus planipennis adults and extended residual activity from 48 to 120 hours. In growth chamber foliage trials it suppressed adult feeding and caused substantial mortality; field tests are still needed.

ag.title: Preharvest spray of antagonist PZB-0006 cuts sweet cherry postharvest rot
ag.summary: Preharvest spraying of the microbial antagonist PZB-0006 reduced cherry fruit rot during storage. Amplicon sequencing showed the strain colonised fruit surfaces stably and reduced pathogenic taxa, and treated fruit had higher defence enzyme activity. The authors position it as an alternative to synthetic fungicides; the PubMed abstract does not give percentage decay reduction.

ag.title: BRRI dhan102 tops 34 Bangladeshi rice cultivars for main plus ratoon yield
ag.summary: In the irrigated boro season, main-crop yields ranged from 4.41 t/ha (BRRI dhan28) to 8.13 t/ha (BRRI dhan102), and 11 cultivars showed moderate to high ratooning ability when cut at 20 cm stubble. Combined main and ratoon yield was highest for BRRI dhan102 (8.64 t/ha) and Tata Miniket (8.50 t/ha). This was a single-location trial, and the authors call for multilocation testing.

ag.title: Phosphate-solubilising Talaromyces pinophilus Y29 boosts maize growth in pots
ag.summary: Strain Y29 released 753.3, 187.0 and 61.5 mg/L of phosphate from calcium, iron and aluminium phosphates, driven by lactic, oxalic and citric acid secretion. Metabolomics pointed to the TCA and glyoxylate pathways, with an isocitrate lyase gene as a candidate. In amended soil, inoculation raised maize dry weight 19.6 to 29.1% and root length 40.5 to 55.2%, in pot trials only.

ag.title: A nodule Bacillus doubled soybean nodules when paired with Bradyrhizobium
ag.summary: Of five non-rhizobial nodule endophytes, Bacillus altitudinis NRE-208 co-inoculated with Bradyrhizobium japonicum RE-11 doubled nodule number and raised acetylene reduction (nitrogen fixation) by 134.7% versus RE-11 alone in gnotobiotic pots. A six-member consortium beat it in only four of eleven traits, and substrate profiling found no carbon-niche partitioning. The authors caution that putative shared metabolites are a shortlist, not a validated biostimulant.

ag.title: Endophyte benefits in Kernza and wheat depend on host genotype, not lab traits
ag.summary: Five endophytes chosen from 21 strains for growth-promoting traits were tested on two wheat cultivars, two perennial ryegrasses and the perennial grain Kernza (Thinopyrum intermedium). Only Streptomyces phaeochromogenes ISE-4 increased shoot and root dry weight, and only in Kernza and wheat cv. Euforia; the rest were neutral or negative. Lab screening traits did not predict benefit, a caution for bioinoculant selection.

ag.title: Review: tomato brown rugose fruit virus and the mite-borne tomato fruit blotch virus pose opposite threats
ag.summary: ToBRFV, a well-studied tobamovirus, has disrupted tomato production worldwide by overcoming the long-durable Tm-22 resistance gene and spreading efficiently by contact. Tomato fruit blotch virus, a little-known blunervirus carried by eriophyid mites, moves poorly within plants and gives variable symptoms tied to vector dynamics. The review contrasts how each challenges disease management.

ag.title: Systematic review: aflatoxin in Ethiopian groundnut reaches 11,900 µg/kg
ag.summary: A PRISMA review of Ethiopian studies found maize aflatoxin B<sub>1</sub> up to 381.6 µg/kg, groundnut up to 1,990.86 µg/kg B<sub>1</sub> and 11,900 µg/kg total aflatoxins, and red pepper and berbere up to 98.99 µg/kg. Milk aflatoxin M<sub>1</sub> ranged from 0.003 to 4.98 µg/L, with several samples above the EU limit. The authors call for better postharvest handling, resistant varieties and surveillance.

methods: Coverage window: 14 to 15 November 2026 (about 48 hours; the previous issue was 2026-11-14, so nothing was skipped). Items were found by PubMed searches filtered on entry date (14 to 15 November) across plant science, genomics, pathology, entomology and microbiology journals, and every date comes from the PubMed record because publisher sites and news sites were not reachable directly from this session. This was a weekend, so major-journal output was thin and today's briefing is journal-only: web searches surfaced no ag or biotech news reliably dated to the window (the Soilcea CRISPR citrus rootstock approval resurfaced but dates from April 2026, and a reported UK Phytoform potato release could not be confirmed against the Defra notice). Five items carry only a month or year in PubMed (Molecular Plant Pathology, The Plant Genome, Physiologia Plantarum, The Scientific World Journal) and are dated to their 14 November PubMed entry; the wheat grain spatial transcriptomics paper is dated 12 November by the journal but entered PubMed on 14 November. Arabidopsis-only results (ANAC030) are flagged, as are controlled-environment, pot, seedling and laboratory results without field data, developer-run software benchmarks and a short commentary. No preprints or company claims are included. Items covered in the 12 to 14 November issues (including maize H2A.Z, strawberry autotetraploids, the NLR screen for turnip mosaic virus and the cotton GEX1 haploid study) were skipped, as were catch-up records whose publication dates fall in October or early November.
